issue.title: JAX-RS subresources do not work in the native mode

labels.name: triage/out-of-date
labels.description: This issue/PR is no longer valid or relevant

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
JAX-RS subresources are not recognized in the native mode.

**Expected behavior**
They work as expected

**Actual behavior**
An exception like the one below is thrown:
```
019-09-30 13:38:04,247 ERROR [io.qua.resteasy] (vert.x-worker-thread-1) Unhandled Exception: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: RESTEASY003895: Unable to find a public constructor for class org.acme.jwt.LottoNumbersResource
```
**To Reproduce**

Remove [this override](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-quickstarts/blob/development/security-jwt-quickstart/src/test/java/org/acme/jwt/TokenSecuredResourceIT.java#L13) in the using-jwt-auth guide.
Note a subresource locator is [here](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-quickstarts/blob/development/security-jwt-quickstart/src/main/java/org/acme/jwt/TokenSecuredResource.java#L127), the actual subresource handler is [here](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-quickstarts/blob/development/security-jwt-quickstart/src/main/java/org/acme/jwt/LottoNumbersResource.java) (adding an explicit default constructor does not help)

body: +1 same happens for me `1.0.1.Final`. Are there any updates on this?
@asoldano could you confirm that what is described above should work?

Some more investigation on this:

Apparently the issue is caused by removal of the sub-resource at build time. When I use `resourceContext.getResource(MySubResource.class)` and at the same time annotate `MySubResource` with `@Unremovable` (or use an unused, dummy injection of `@Inject MySubResource mySubResource`), then it works as expected.

From the logs:

```
2020-02-06 08:11:19,374 WARN  [io.qua.arc.run.ArcRecorder] (executor-thread-1) Bean matching class com.sebastian_daschner.MySubResource was marked as unused and removed during build.
```

So, I guess we could resolve this by taking the sub-resource creation via `ResourceContext#getResource(Class)` into account?
